open_gaps: K7 is red, and it was already red before this candidate made any changes: the K7-basis receipt (baseline snapshot fc8531e902b5, same base commit 63d90ce, before the candidate's own dirty edits) shows the identical two failing tests. Because src/hoh/**, tests/** and pyproject.toml are explicitly out of scope for this run (a concurrent d1 run owns them in a different worktree), this candidate had no permitted way to fix the regression itself. The development document's 'Behaviour to preserve' section asserts 'python3 -m pytest -q currently passes (353 tests collected and green) and must stay green' -- that premise was already false when this run started, which is worth surfacing to whoever owns sequencing between d1 and d2, since it means the two runs are not actually isolated at the test-suite level even though they are isolated at the file level.

The two failing tests (test_D4_start_rejects_a_non_git_directory in tests/test_review_findings.py, and test_not_a_git_repo in tests/test_workspace.py) both concern hoh.workspace.is_git_repo / WorkspaceError and hoh.cli's non-git-repo rejection path -- exactly the kind of source module a concurrent d1 run (scoped to src/hoh/**) could plausibly be mid-edit on. This is an observation about likely cause, not verified against d1's own worktree, which QA was not asked to inspect and did not touch.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md's UNVERIFIED note for pydantic ('this repository does not vendor pydantic and holds no local, repo-relative copy of its LICENSE file') was spot-checked and holds: no pydantic files and no .venv/site-packages directory exist anywhere under the candidate's own tree.
summary: Criteria K1-K6, K8 and K9 all pass on both the receipts and QA's independent re-execution: the seven governance files exist, are substantive, correctly cross-reference sources or use the UNVERIFIED marker for every licensing claim, declare exactly the one real third-party import, name the required CHANGELOG interface changes, leak no private trace, and leave lint clean -- with LICENSE itself honestly left unresolved rather than guessed, matching the spec's central constraint. K7 (pytest) is a genuine FAIL (2 of 353 tests red), but candidate-bound evidence -- an identical basis-receipt failure plus a byte-identical src/tests diff against the pre-candidate baseline -- shows this regression predates and is untouched by the candidate's own out-of-scope-respecting change, which added only the seven permitted files.
